Canberra: Pacific Linguistics 555.
tone_statements.quote: Phu Kha has three tones with values 31, 35, 33, as well as a few words with the tone value 53. Several of these tone values can be accompanied with sharp glottal constriction at the end of the syllable. This feature is still easily perceived and has not as yet resulted in a tense/lax voice quality contrast as has happened in many Yi languages.

sources.citation: Pelkey, Jamin R. 2005. Puzzling over Phula: toward the synthesis and statement of a sub-branch. Linguistics of the Tibeto-Burman Area 28(2): 43-78.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. General Phula phonology remarks only: 'Most known Phula languages have a tense-lax phonation contrast, and some retain consonant finals. Phula languages usually have five tonemes and utilize contour tonal contrasts' (p. 58); footnote notes Fried (2000:27) lists a fifth glottalized tone for Phukhla while Edmondson (2003:308) interprets it differently.
